how.title: How it works
how.intro: Three steps from a locked drive to your files in Finder. The one-time setup takes about a minute.

steps.title: Drag to Applications
steps.text: Open the DMG and drag Unbit into your Applications folder. It lives in the menu bar, not the Dock.

steps.title: Grant Full Disk Access
steps.text: A short guide shows you where to switch it on in System Settings. You only do this once.

steps.title: Plug in and unlock
steps.text: Unbit spots the drive automatically. Enter the password or recovery key, and the drive opens in Finder.

readOnly.title: Read-only, by design
readOnly.text: Unbit attaches the unlocked drive to macOS as read-only. Nothing is ever written back, so your files, and the drive's BitLocker setup, stay exactly as Windows left them. Copy what you need, then eject.

features.title: Everything you need, nothing you don't
features.intro: A small, focused menu bar app for one job: getting to the files on a BitLocker drive.

items.title: No drivers or macFUSE
items.text: No kernel extensions and no third-party file system layers. Unbit uses the disk image support already built into macOS.

items.title: Decrypts on demand
items.text: Only the parts macOS actually reads are decrypted, as they're read. No waiting for a full copy of the drive.

items.title: Detects drives automatically
items.text: Plug in a drive and it appears in Unbit right away. Unplug it and Unbit tidies up on its own.

items.title: Safe eject
items.text: One click closes the drive and ejects it, so you know when it's safe to unplug. Quitting closes an open drive first.

items.title: Remembers drives, if you want
items.text: Tick "Remember this drive" and the code is stored encrypted in your macOS keychain, never anywhere else.

items.title: Updates itself, notarized by Apple
items.text: Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple. New versions arrive through signed automatic updates.

groups.title: Opening your drive
items: Password or recovery key – Type the password or the 48-digit key, paste it, or drop the key file from Windows.
Clear progress – See each step while the drive opens, and get a plain explanation and a fix if something fails.
Several drives at once – Open more than one drive, each with its own usage and activity.
Opens known drives automatically – Optional, using the code saved in your keychain, and with Touch ID if you like.
Notifications – Hear when a drive connects, opens or can't be opened.
Finder and last folder – Optionally open Finder when the drive opens, and return to the last folder you used.
Try a demo drive – A built-in, made-up drive with sample files lets you see how Unbit works without a real BitLocker drive.

groups.title: Find and copy files
items: Search the drive – Look up file and folder names, and preview results with Quick Look.
Copy basket – Collect files from the search results and copy them to your Mac in one go.
Favorites and recent files – Jump to your favorite folders and the files you used last.
Copy to Mac – Choose what happens when a file already exists: ask, rename or skip.
Copy only what changed – Skip identical files, so copying a folder again only brings what is new.
Verify copies – An optional SHA-256 check of every copied file, with a clear Verified status.
Copy report – See what was copied, skipped or failed, and save the report as a file.
Speed and time left – Follow MB/s and the estimated time remaining in the panel and the menu bar.
Drag files out – Drag files from the search results, recent files or the basket to Finder or into a mail. The drive is only read.

groups.title: Safe by design
items: Read-only – Nothing is ever written to your drive.
Safe eject – Eject with one click, and optionally after copying, when the Mac sleeps or locks, or after a period of inactivity.
Drive health warning – Get a warning if the drive itself reports that it is failing.
Cleans up after itself – If Unbit ever quits unexpectedly, leftovers are removed the next time it starts.
Erase all data – One command removes Unbit's settings, saved codes and statistics from this Mac.
Private by default – No accounts, no analytics, and saved codes stay in your keychain.

groups.title: Menu bar and looks
items: Live menu bar – A lock icon shows the state, and the percentage while a copy runs.
Icon, colors and size – Choose the icon style, a color theme, the density and the text size; light and dark follow macOS.
Global shortcut – Open the panel from any app with a key combination you choose.
Keyboard shortcuts – Refresh, search, copy and quit without touching the mouse.
Start at login – Optional, so Unbit is ready in the menu bar.
Shortcuts, Siri and Spotlight – Open and eject drives from Shortcuts. Codes are never passed through Shortcuts.

groups.title: Help and transparency
items: Errors in plain language – Every error explains what happened and offers the next step, with a help page in your language.
Send an error report – One click opens a pre-filled email with an anonymous report. You decide whether to send it.
What happens to my drive? – A short explanation in the welcome card, with a link to the step-by-step guide.
Your own statistics – Drives opened and files copied, kept only on this Mac and reset whenever you like.
About and what's new – Version, news and the privacy statement are one click away.

privacy.title: Your drive never leaves your Mac
privacy.text: Decryption happens entirely on your Mac. Your password, recovery key and files are never sent anywhere. The app has no accounts, analytics or tracking. The only thing Unbit fetches from the internet is its daily update check.

items.q: Should I use the password or the recovery key?
items.a: Either one works. The password is the one chosen when BitLocker was turned on for the drive. The recovery key is the 48-digit key (8 groups of 6 digits) that Windows asked you to save at the same time, for example to a Microsoft account, a file or a printout. Pick whichever you have in the app.

items.q: Why does Unbit need Full Disk Access?
items.a: To decrypt the drive, Unbit has to read the raw, encrypted data straight from the external drive. macOS only allows that for apps with Full Disk Access. Unbit uses it to read the drive you choose and nothing else.

items.q: Can I write to the drive?
items.a: No. Unbit is read-only by design and never writes to the drive. You can open files and copy them to your Mac. To change files on the drive, use Windows.

items.q: Does it work on Apple silicon and Intel Macs?
items.a: Yes. Unbit is a universal app that runs natively on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs with macOS 13 Ventura or later.

External drives encrypted with BitLocker or BitLocker To Go on Windows 7 or later – USB sticks, external SSDs and HDDs – using AES-CBC (with or without the Elephant diffuser) or AES-XTS, with 128- or 256-bit keys. Once unlocked, macOS reads the file system on the drive itself. Internal disks aren't supported.

Only if you tick "Remember this drive on this Mac". The code is then saved encrypted in your macOS keychain after a successful unlock, and you can forget it at any time from the gear menu. It's never sent anywhere.

trial.label: Free trial
trial.unbit: Not needed – the full app is free

write.label: Write support
write.unbit: No. Read-only by design: open files and copy them to your Mac

drivers.label: Drivers and system access
drivers.unbit: No kernel extension or macFUSE. Uses disk image support built into macOS. Needs Full Disk Access

silicon.label: Apple silicon
silicon.unbit: Yes – universal app for Apple silicon and Intel

privacy.label: Privacy and activation
privacy.unbit: Decryption happens on your Mac. No accounts, analytics or tracking. Only a daily update check goes online

extras.label: Extras
extras.unbit: Menu bar app with automatic drive detection, safe eject and optional keychain memory. Does not encrypt drives or change BitLocker settings

iboysoft.tagline: Commercial app with read-write access and BitLocker encryption.
iboysoft.intro: iBoysoft BitLocker for Mac is a paid app that unlocks BitLocker drives on macOS and can also write to them. Unbit covers a narrower job – opening a drive and copying files off it – for free and without drivers.

cells.price: Paid: US$39.95 monthly, US$79.95 yearly (both auto-renewing) or US$159.95 one-time with lifetime upgrades. Per Mac, excl. VAT
cells.trial: Yes, but the trial can only browse and preview files. Mounting the drive in Finder needs the paid version
cells.write: Yes – read and write, including editing, renaming and deleting files
cells.drivers: The Finder (Volume Mounter) mode needs a system extension. On Apple silicon the vendor documents switching to Reduced Security in Recovery. A File Manager mode works without it
cells.silicon: Yes – M1 to M5 and Intel (with the system extension enabled)
cells.privacy: Activation requires internet access, according to the vendor's purchase FAQ
cells.extras: Can also encrypt drives with BitLocker, supports keychain auto-unlock. NTFS, FAT32 and exFAT

themPick: need to edit, add or delete files on a BitLocker drive from your Mac
want to encrypt external drives with BitLocker on macOS
are fine with a paid licence and a one-time system extension setup
unbitPick: only need to open a drive and copy your files off it
prefer not to enable system extensions or lower startup security on Apple silicon
want a free app with no licence key or trial limits

faq.q: Is there a free version of iBoysoft BitLocker for Mac?
faq.a: iBoysoft offers a trial that can browse and preview files on the drive, but mounting it in Finder needs a paid licence. Unbit is free and opens the drive in Finder, read-only.

faq.q: Does iBoysoft BitLocker for Mac need Reduced Security on Apple silicon?
faq.a: For its Finder-mounting mode, the vendor says system extensions must be enabled, which on Apple silicon includes selecting Reduced Security in Recovery. Its File Manager mode works without a system extension. Unbit uses no kernel extension, so your startup security stays unchanged.

hasleo.tagline: Low-cost commercial app that reads, writes and encrypts.
hasleo.intro: Hasleo BitLocker Anywhere for Mac is a paid all-in-one tool that can mount drives read-write or read-only, and also encrypt and decrypt them. Unbit is the lighter option when you just want to read your files.

cells.price: Paid: US$19.98 (listed as reduced from US$39.95) for a one-Mac Professional licence, excl. VAT. Free lifetime upgrades
cells.trial: A free/trial version exists that a licence key turns into the full version. We could not verify its limits
cells.write: Yes – mounts drives read-write or read-only
cells.drivers: On Apple silicon the vendor's support forum describes enabling Reduced Security and allowing kernel extensions to install it. Full Disk Access is also required
cells.silicon: Yes – Intel and Apple silicon (M1 to M4 listed)
cells.extras: Encrypts and decrypts drives, changes the password, exports the recovery key and startup key. NTFS, FAT and exFAT. Command line only in a separate edition

themPick: need to write to a BitLocker drive from your Mac
want to encrypt, decrypt or change the password of drives on macOS
are fine with a paid licence and a more involved setup on Apple silicon
unbitPick: just want to read your files and copy them to your Mac
want to avoid kernel extensions and Reduced Security
prefer a free app with nothing to buy or activate

faq.q: Can Hasleo BitLocker Anywhere for Mac write to drives?
faq.a: Yes. According to the vendor it can mount BitLocker drives read-write or read-only. Unbit only ever mounts drives read-only.

faq.q: Is Hasleo BitLocker Anywhere for Mac free?
faq.a: No. The vendor sells a paid Professional licence for one Mac and lists a free/trial version that a licence key unlocks. Unbit is free.

uubyte.tagline: Paid reader that can enable write access after unlocking.
uubyte.intro: UUByte BitLocker Geeker is a paid app for unlocking BitLocker drives on a Mac, with optional write access. Unbit is a free, read-only alternative that avoids the kernel extension steps.

cells.price: Paid: US$29.95 for a 1-year plan, US$39.95 lifetime for one Mac or US$59.95 lifetime for 8 Macs. 30-day money-back guarantee listed
cells.write: Yes – after unlocking you can view and copy files, and write access is switched on with an Enable Write button
cells.drivers: The vendor's Apple silicon guide asks you to grant Full Disk Access, allow user management of kernel extensions, update the system extension and restart
cells.silicon: Yes – the vendor has a guide for M1, M2, M3 and M4 Macs
cells.macos: macOS Sierra up to Tahoe, according to the purchase page
cells.extras: Keychain auto-unlock. NTFS, FAT32 and exFAT

themPick: want the option to write to a BitLocker drive from your Mac
are fine with a paid licence
are comfortable following the kernel extension steps for Apple silicon
unbitPick: only need to read files and copy them off the drive
want to skip kernel extensions and restarts
prefer a free app with no licence key

faq.a: Not necessarily. The vendor says that after unlocking you can view and copy files, and that write access is enabled with an Enable Write button. Unbit is always read-only.

faq.q: Does UUByte BitLocker Geeker need kernel extensions on Apple silicon?
faq.a: The vendor's Apple silicon guide includes allowing user management of kernel extensions and updating the system extension. Unbit uses no kernel extension or macFUSE.

anylinuxfs.tagline: Free open-source command-line tool with read-write support.
anylinuxfs.intro: anylinuxfs is a free, open-source command-line tool that mounts Linux-supported file systems on Apple silicon Macs, including BitLocker drives. Unbit is a ready-to-use Mac app for the same unlocking job, with no Terminal and no virtual machine.

cells.write: Yes – read-write by default, read-only mounting can be selected
cells.drivers: No kernel extensions and no lowering of system security. It runs a lightweight virtual machine and shares the drive over NFS
cells.silicon: Apple silicon only. Intel Macs are not supported
cells.unlock: BitLocker volumes with NTFS or FAT32. The project documents using the recovery key as the passphrase
cells.privacy: Runs locally. The drive is shared only to your own Mac (localhost) by default
cells.extras: Command-line tool installed with Homebrew. The drive appears to macOS as a network drive. Also supports ext4, btrfs, LUKS, ZFS and more. Known issue: Microsoft Word cannot edit files directly on a mounted drive

themPick: are comfortable with Terminal and Homebrew
need free read-write access to a BitLocker drive
also work with Linux file systems such as ext4, btrfs or LUKS
unbitPick: want a normal Mac app instead of a command-line tool
use an Intel Mac or need the same app on both Intel and Apple silicon
want a read-only mount so nothing can be written to the drive

faq.q: Does anylinuxfs work on Intel Macs?
faq.a: No. The project states that only Apple silicon Macs are supported. Unbit is a universal app that runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
anylinuxfs itself is a command-line utility. Its README points to a separate graphical front end. Unbit is a menu bar app that detects the drive and asks for the password or recovery key.

parallels.tagline: Run Windows in a virtual machine and unlock the drive there.
parallels.intro: Parallels Desktop is a virtualization app. Many people use a Windows virtual machine to unlock a BitLocker drive, because Windows supports BitLocker natively. It works, but it is a much bigger setup than Unbit.

cells.price: Paid: annual subscription, or a one-time purchase for the Standard edition. A Windows licence is not included
cells.write: Handled by Windows inside the virtual machine, so it behaves like on a Windows PC
cells.drivers: No BitLocker driver on macOS. You connect the external drive (USB) to the Windows virtual machine, where it is no longer visible on the Mac
cells.silicon: Yes – macOS Big Sur or later on Apple silicon, macOS Catalina or later on Intel
cells.unlock: Password or recovery key, entered in Windows
cells.extras: A full Windows virtual machine that also runs Windows apps. Needs a Windows installation and licence, plus disk space and memory for the virtual machine

themPick: already run Windows in Parallels Desktop
want full Windows behaviour for the drive, including writing
also need Windows apps on your Mac
unbitPick: just want to open one drive without installing Windows
do not want to buy a Windows licence or run a virtual machine
want the drive to show up in Finder like any other disk

faq.q: Can Parallels Desktop open BitLocker drives on a Mac?
faq.a: Yes, indirectly. You connect the external drive (for example a USB stick) to a Windows virtual machine and unlock it with Windows' own BitLocker support. It is a general virtualization workflow rather than a dedicated BitLocker feature.

faq.q: Do I need a Windows licence to use Parallels Desktop?
faq.a: According to Parallels, a Windows licence is not included and you need one to activate Windows. Unbit needs no Windows at all.
